//: NAMED, SHRINK-ONLY ledger for check-dependent-adapts-on-host-move.
SUBJECT: the founder's principle, 2026-08-21 — 'elements should propagate when one
moves, all contexts'. One cell per (dependent family, moving host), one verdict per
cell: PROPAGATES, REFUSES, or SILENT. The narrative form is ADR-0344.
PINNED 2026-08-21 (lane PROP1) AT THE FIRST MEASURED READING — 64 cells,
19 PROPAGATES / 6 REFUSES / 39 SILENT. Every PROPAGATES and REFUSES marker in this
file was grep-verified against HEAD before the ledger was written, and every 'absent'
probe on a SILENT cell was verified to be genuinely absent. A ledger pinned above or
below its own gate's reading is not a ratchet — the first is free slots, the second is
permanently unsatisfiable (move-propagation.json records that exact draft mistake).
WHY SILENT IS THE ONLY FINDING. An honest REFUSES is a valid answer: the product
does not adapt the dependent AND says so by name with a reason (C74). SILENT is the
defect — nothing happens and nothing is said, so 'there is no dependent here' and
'the dependent was never wired' arrive at the reader as the SAME VALUE (C78 §1.4).
That is exactly what the founder saw: a wall moved 19.444 m and the floor finish
neither followed nor refused.
SHRINK-ONLY, CHECKED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. A new SILENT cell exits 3. A SILENT cell
whose probe says the defect is GONE is STALE and also exits 3 — debt that has been
paid must leave the ledger in the commit that pays it. And a PROPAGATES cell whose
wiring evidence stops resolving is a REGRESSION TO SILENT, counted as a finding on
top of the ledger, so it cannot be absorbed.
THE ONE CELL THIS LANE CLOSED: 'floor finish × wall' and 'ceiling finish × wall' were
SILENT for every finish whose relationship was never recorded at creation. Closed by
§FINISH-FOLLOW-LATE-ATTRIBUTION (L-2090); the cells now carry the hook itself as
evidence, so deleting the repair turns the gate red rather than turning the product
quiet again.
⚠ THE HEADER ABOVE WAS WRONG ON ITS FIRST WRITE AND THE GATE CAUGHT IT. It was
hand-typed as '52 cells, 27 SILENT' before the ledger was finished; the first run
read 64 / 39. Recorded rather than quietly corrected, because 'the prose number was
transcribed instead of counted' is the exact defect shape this repository logs most
often, and it happened inside the artefact built to stop it. Read the gate's output,
never this paragraph.
NEGATIVE CONTROL, executed 2026-08-21 before this ledger was trusted (C74 §6.2 — an
arm never watched failing is UNPROVEN): the 'floor finish × wall' cell's marker
'new FloorHostDependencyTracker(' was temporarily changed to a symbol that does not
exist. The gate went to RC=3 with 'REGRESSED-TO-SILENT: floor finish × wall', 40
findings against 39. The marker was restored and the gate returned to RC=1 at 39.
ARM A therefore discriminates; it is not counting its own ledger back to itself.
§GRAPH115 (2026-08-26, ADR-0374): 'plumbing × wall' left this ledger — the anchor
field the SILENT note said could not be expressed now exists, minted at placement,
and the follower is wired in initTools. 39 → 38.
EXIT CONDITION — declaredSilent reaches [] when every dependent family either adapts
to every host that can move it, or refuses BY NAME. Reducing a cell from SILENT to
REFUSES is a legitimate and often correct fix: narrowing a claim to the truth is a
fix; leaving it silent is not.

cells.note: FinishHostDependencyTracker re-projects the boundary and writes it back through UpdateFloorBoundaryCommand as a STRUCTURAL_CASCADE child (one undo). Finishes whose relationship was never recorded at creation are re-attributed against the moved wall alone (§FINISH-FOLLOW-LATE-ATTRIBUTION, L-2090).
The floor's twin, through the same base class and the same hook — C79 §7.4 forbids the two finish families diverging.

Two live paths: SlabDependencyTracker re-resolves the region sketch, and SlabWallConnectivityService dispatches CascadeWallBaselineCommand as a STRUCTURAL_CASCADE. The tracker's own write-back is a direct store write, not a command — see ADR-0344 §P6 shortfall.
The level-rebuild callback queries slabs by level and calls triggerRebuild. One of exactly TWO kinds the reconcile reaches.
The stair's void follows and the host slab rebuilds. The slab's own polygon is untouched — only the hosted opening moves.
The level-rebuild callback rebuilds each delivered wall id. The OTHER of the two kinds the reconcile reaches.

RoofDependencyTracker re-asks the region question at the stored anchor and writes UpdateRoofBoundaryCommand. NOTE: dispatched WITHOUT source metadata, so a roof follow costs a SECOND undo — ADR-0344 §P6 shortfall.
RoomTopologyObserver schedules a debounced re-detect; the wall command invalidates the boundary conclusions so a stale ring is never read as current.
Wired: a slab add/update/remove schedules a re-detect on its level. NO test in the tree drives this arm — wiring proven, behaviour UNPROVEN.
A room-bounding-line edit schedules a re-detect on its level. Also undriven by any test.
The best-wired pair in the product: baseline, height and thickness all re-anchor, once per opening, and the executed gate check-propagation-trackers-reach drives all three branches.

The BASE-OFFSET term only: a slab base-offset change moves the host wall's base plane, which no wall-record diff can see, and the trackers subscribe to that term directly. A slab POLYGON change reaches no opening.
Classified DETERMINED-HOSTED: re-rendered by the host wall's own rebuild via its opening render map, with no independent reconcile consumer.

Direct edit refits openings inside UpdateWallBaselineCommand; a wall moved BY ANOTHER wall's move rebases them inside CascadeWallBaselineCommand, as a STRUCTURAL_CASCADE. This is the path the founder's log shows working.
Move a stair and the SAME opening moves with it, inside the stair command's own frame — so it is one undo by construction.
The rail path is re-sampled from the host at build time on bim-stair-updated. No record write-back, so no command and no undo entry — correct here, because nothing authored is being changed.

AnnotationDependencyGraph subscribes to StoreEventBus and re-resolves every wall reference on flush. WallStore is the ONLY emitter that forwards prevState. NOTE: zero test files reference AnnotationDependencyGraph — the resolver is pinned, the subscription is not.

ReseatLevelElementsCommand re-seats position.y for exactly these three families when a floor/ceiling FINISH is created, updated, re-layered or removed — composed into the parent command's undo. It is NOT reached by a wall move or a level elevation change.

The ONE surviving generic channel: pryzm-dep-cascade, listened to by initDependencyCascade, routing sitsOn/supports ONLY. Priorities 2-5 reach the listener and are dropped on the floor by design, because the bespoke trackers own them.

DETERMINED-STRANDED by name, plus a user-facing toast naming the level, the delta and the roof: 'Level X moved N m but roof Y did not follow … Rebuild the roof or adjust its base offset.' The strongest refusal in the matrix — it reaches the USER, not just the console.
DETERMINED-STRANDED with the C72 §5.1 / PR-07 reason: the level-rebuild callback reaches Wall and Slab only, so a beam keeps its old elevation and the shortfall is announced per level.
Same seam, same named refusal, enumerated by name in StrandedKind.
Same seam. 'CurtainWall' is a named member of StrandedKind.
Same seam. 'Stair' is a named member of StrandedKind.
Same seam. 'Furniture' is a named member of StrandedKind and is probed by SpatialAuthority, so the refusal is reached rather than fallen through.
UpdateSlabPolygonCommand notifies no dependent of any kind. A slab boundary edit reaches nothing.
No room→slab edge exists in either direction of adaptation.
RoofDependencyTracker subscribes to the wall store only.
No stair→roof edge.
A roof records the bounding-wall SET and an anchor, never a room.

The host reference EXISTS — BeamData.startSupportId / startSupportType 'wall' — written by AssignBeamSupportsCommand and read by the AI read-model and the rule engine. No mover reads it. C70 §4.2 in its purest form: reference present, consumer absent.
No slab subscription in the beam package.
No stair subscription in the beam package.
No subscription. SlabColumnCoupling.resolveSlabBaseOffsetForPoint is a pure read-only query consulted at authoring and build time only; nothing re-invokes it when the host moves.
A column's base offset is resolved from the slab beneath it AT CREATION and never re-resolved when that slab moves.
No stair subscription in the column package.
CurtainWallTypes declares NO host-wall field at all, so the relationship cannot even be expressed. Panels do follow their own curtain wall (CurtainPanelSyncHandler); the curtain wall follows nothing.
No slab subscription.
No stair subscription.
StairVerticalSpanResolver and StairLevelSpanChange are pure resolvers invoked at create and parameter time; neither subscribes to anything.
A stair pierces its horizontal hosts at create/param time and is never re-resolved when one of them moves.

FurnitureData carries no wallId, no hostId and no roomId. A wardrobe against a wall has no relationship to lose — the edge cannot be expressed at all. THE LARGEST GAP IN THIS MATRIX by user-visible impact.
Same: no host field, no subscription.
RoomContentsService reads furniture INTO a room query; it is a read service and writes no element.

LightingData declares hostId, and the file itself records that exactly one writer and one loader-reader exist and that no placement path sets it. The one refusal that DOES exist (§L-1032) is about the fixture's own storey change, not a host move.

Lighting is absent from SpatialAuthority's probe list, so it classifies UNDETERMINED, is delivered fail-open, and is dropped by the level-rebuild callback with no else and no log. A handler EXISTS and early-returns silently — the worst shape in the matrix, because it looks handled.

roomId is resolved from plan position at create/move time only; LightingStore states it is left alone deliberately because re-deriving it needs a room set the store cannot see. Deliberate, but unannounced at the moment it matters.

§GRAPH115 / ADR-0374 (2026-08-26): PlumbingFixtureData.wallAnchor is minted at placement from the tool's own snap target (plan + 3-D), and WallAnchorDependencyTracker reseats every agreeing fixture through ONE ReseatWallAnchoredElementsCommand dispatched as a STRUCTURAL_CASCADE child (one Ctrl+Z). A fixture the user moved since anchoring is DETACHED audibly, never teleported; an off-host reseat REFUSES with both numbers; a host delete keeps the fixture and detaches it inside the delete gesture. Pre-existing fixtures carry no anchor until re-placed (no proximity re-attribution, C79 §2.2).
Same silent drop as lighting at the level-rebuild callback.
HandrailData.hostKind is 'stair' | 'slab' — it cannot be 'wall', so a wall-mounted handrail is inexpressible.

AUTHORED-BUT-UNWIRED, and the clearest case in the repo: buildStairHandrailCascadeRule is fully written and synthesises handrail.recompute on stair.move — its only caller is registerCrossHandlers, which has ZERO production callers, and CascadeRunner is instantiated only in tests. MoveStairCommand.affectedStores does not name handrail. Deletion of a stair DOES orphan-clean its handrails; motion does nothing.
A stair railing follows its stair and nothing else.
FinishHostDependencyTracker wires exactly one store subscription — the wall store. There is no slab subscription anywhere in the package.
ceilingStore is not among SpatialAuthority's eight probed stores, so a ceiling id is delivered fail-open and dropped without a log.
RoomFinishSyncService listens to bim-room-updated but writes only finishSpec — material and colour. No boundary or sketch re-derivation exists on this path, and its guard early-returns with no log.
A finish is seated ON its slab at creation (resolveFinishSeating) and re-seated when the FINISH changes — never when the SLAB moves or its boundary changes.
Same fail-open drop as the ceiling: floorStore is not probed by SpatialAuthority.
RoomTopologyObserver.attach subscribes to wall, curtain-wall, room-bounding-line, slab and column stores. It has no level subscription and no reconcile listener.

PARTIAL, and classified by what it fails to do: the refresh writes only `parameters`, so the label and area update while the ANCHOR strands. The tag is bound to a baked point reference, and AnnotationDependencyGraph explicitly skips point refs, so it is not in the associativity index at all.
Same mechanism: area drift refreshes the text, the position stays at the old centroid.

The AUTODIMENSION executor can only mint wall/door/window references, so no auto-dimension ever carries a slab id and the graph lookup returns nothing. A hand-picked slope dimension is the only slab-referencing case.
NO store in the repo emits elementType 'level' on StoreEventBus, so the level branch of the reference resolver is unreachable dead code. The subscriber exists and never fires.

RoomStore does emit on the bus, but no production code mints a room StableReference and the resolver has no room branch — a room ref would fall to its cached position. The lookup returns undefined and the handler early-returns with no log.

openingStore is not in SpatialAuthority's probe list, so an opening id classifies UNDETERMINED and is delivered to the rebuild callback — which drops it at `const wall = store.getById(id); if (wall) {` with no else and no log, even though window.openingStore is populated and reachable.
